news.headline: Rosalind Advisors Converts Series E Preferred and Distributes Shares In Kind to Fund LPs
news.summary: Director-affiliated Rosalind Opportunities Fund I converted 36.27 Series E preferred shares into 3,627 common shares and distributed 27,502 common shares in kind to limited partners to meet redemption requests. It is a fund-level distribution rather than an open-market sale, but it adds a little freely tradable supply while the stock drifts lower.

news.headline: BTIG Reiterates Buy and $21 Target on Delcath Ahead of Q3
news.summary: BTIG's Ryan Zimmerman reiterated his Buy rating and $21 target in the run-up to Q3 results, the latest in an unbroken string of Buy ratings. TipRanks shows all covering analysts at Buy with an average target of about $24.50 (range $21-$32).

news.headline: H.C. Wainwright Reiterates Buy, Street-High $32 Target; Consensus Stays Unanimously Bullish
news.summary: H.C. Wainwright's Swayampakula Ramakanth reaffirmed Buy with a $32 target after the firm's September investor conference. All brokers covering Delcath rate it Strong Buy, with Zacks' short-term consensus near $21.80 and broader averages around $22.50-$24.50.

news.headline: Delcath Grants Inducement RSUs to Four New Hires as Commercial Build-Out Continues
news.summary: Delcath granted a total of 34,000 restricted stock units (grant date September 1) to four employees who joined in July or August 2026, vesting over three years. The dilution is immaterial, but it signals continued hiring to support center activations; it remains the company's most recent press release.

news.headline: Analysis: HEPZATO Growth Is Real, But 340B Pricing, Slow Hospital Onboarding and Heavy Spend Cap the Margin Story
news.summary: A widely circulated sell-side-style review argued that HEPZATO volume growth of roughly 30% and the raised $104M-$108M guidance are solid, but flagged 340B/NDRA pricing pressure, slow hospital onboarding timelines and rising R&D and SG&A as the reasons profitability is advancing more slowly than the top line. It framed the stock as a growth story that has to prove operating leverage in Q3 and Q4.

news.headline: Delcath Reports Q2 2026: $29.1M Revenue Beats Estimates, FY Guidance Raised to $104M-$108M, DELUMA Doses First Patient
news.summary: Revenue rose to $29.1M from $24.2M (HEPZATO KIT $27.1M, CHEMOSAT $2.0M) on roughly 30% HEPZATO volume growth, with gross margin at 90%, net income of $2.7M and EPS of $0.07 versus an expected loss; FY2026 guidance was raised to $104M-$108M with positive adjusted EBITDA and cash stood at $95.9M with no debt. On the call management reported 31 active centers heading to about 37 by year-end (MD Anderson, Mayo Clinic Scottsdale, UT Southwestern, OHSU Knight, Columbia), first patient dosed in the Phase 2 DELUMA breast cancer trial and 13 centers screening for the mCRC Phase 2.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results, with a possible October preliminary revenue pre-release
catalysts.detail: No date has been announced yet; data providers estimate the Q3 report around November 3, 2026. Last year Delcath pre-released preliminary Q3 revenue around October 20, 2025, so a pre-release in the coming days is plausible but had not appeared as of October 18 (no Q3 call-date announcement yet either). This is the first check on whether HEPZATO volumes and center activations are tracking the raised $104M-$108M FY guidance, whether that range gets lifted again, and whether operating leverage shows through after the 340B pricing and spending concerns raised in September commentary.

catalysts.label: ~37 active HEPZATO treatment centers, incl. MD Anderson and Mayo Clinic Scottsdale
catalysts.detail: Delcath exited Q2 with 31 active HEPZATO KIT centers and guided to roughly six additional activations by year-end for about 37. Named additions include MD Anderson, Mayo Clinic Scottsdale, UT Southwestern, OHSU Knight Cancer Institute and Columbia's Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center; UVA Health came online in July. Center count is the most direct driver of near-term revenue, and the September inducement grants for four new hires point to continued commercial staffing behind the build-out.

catalysts.label: FY2026 revenue $104M-$108M and positive adjusted EBITDA
catalysts.detail: Raised guidance implies at least 28% HEPZATO volume growth over 2025, with FY gross margin guided to 86%-89% after Q2 printed 90%. Positive full-year adjusted EBITDA would confirm a self-funding commercial model and, with $95.9M of cash and no debt, remove the dilution overhang that has historically capped the multiple.

catalysts.label: mCRC Phase 2 enrollment progress
catalysts.detail: The company-sponsored Phase 2 of HEPZATO plus trifluridine-tipiracil and bevacizumab versus that regimen alone in third-line liver-dominant metastatic colorectal cancer had 13 centers actively screening as of the Q2 call, with recruitment improving. Enrollment milestones and eventual data would open by far the largest indication in the pipeline, since liver-dominant mCRC dwarfs uveal melanoma in patient numbers.

catalysts.label: DELUMA breast cancer Phase 2 enrollment and data
catalysts.detail: The roughly 90-patient randomized Phase 2 in HER2-negative liver-dominant metastatic breast cancer (PHP-MBC-202, NCT06875128) dosed its first patient in July 2026 at the European Institute of Oncology in Milan and is enrolling across more than 20 US and European sites. Investigator-led retrospective data presented at ESMO Breast Cancer 2026 showed a 60% hepatic partial response rate in heavily pretreated patients, which underpins the trial's thesis. The primary endpoint is hepatic progression-free survival; full enrollment and first efficacy readouts are the next major pipeline catalysts beyond uveal melanoma.

pulse: Delcath closed around $14.05 on Friday, October 16, down about 10% from late September and roughly 19% below the $17.42 August high, with no new company press release since the September 11 inducement grants (October brought only a BTIG Buy reiteration and a Rosalind in-kind share distribution). Coverage remains unanimously Buy with targets of $21-$32, so the pullback reads as pre-earnings positioning amid 340B pricing and spending worries rather than a fundamental change. The next test is imminent: a possible preliminary Q3 revenue release (it came around October 20 last year) and the full Q3 report expected around November 3, measured against the $104M-$108M guidance and the push toward about 37 active centers.
